q.t: Find the common difference of 3, 7, 11, …
q.e: Each term minus the one before: 7 − 3 = 4.

q.t: Find the 10th term of 2, 5, 8, …
q.e: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d = 2 + 9 × 3. From the 1st to the 10th term there are 9 jumps.

o: No — the differences are not equal
q.e: The differences are 5, 10, 20 — they grow, so it is not an AP (each term is doubled, not increased by a fixed amount).

q.t: Find the sum of the first 10 natural numbers.
q.e: Pair first with last: 1 + 10 = 11, and there are 5 such pairs.

q.t: Find the next term of 1.5, 3, 4.5, …
The nth term of an AP with first term a and common difference d is…
q.e: The first term has no jump added; each later term adds one more d, so the nth term has n − 1 of them.

q.t: Find the sum of the first 5 terms of 4, 8, 12, …
An AP has a = 7 and d = −2. Find its 5th term.
Find the number that goes between 4 and 10 to make an AP.
q.e: The middle term of an AP is the average of its neighbours.

q.t: Find the common difference of 10, 6, 2, …
q.e: 6 − 10 = −4. A falling AP has a negative d.

q.t: Which term of 3, 8, 13, … is 78?
How many terms are in 7, 13, 19, …, 205?
q.e: (205 − 7)/6 = 33 jumps, so 34 terms.

q.t: Find the sum of the first 20 odd numbers.
q.e: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². (Or (20/2)(1 + 39).)

q.t: An AP has 3rd term 12 and 7th term 28. Find its 10th term.
q.e: Four jumps from term 3 to term 7 add 16, so d = 4 and a = 4. a₁₀ = 4 + 36.

q.t: Find the sum of the first 10 terms of 2, 7, 12, …
2k + 1, 13 and 5k − 3 are in AP. Find k.
q.e: The middle term is the average: 2 × 13 = (2k + 1) + (5k − 3), so 26 = 7k − 2.

q.t: How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 3?
Find the sum of the first 15 multiples of 8.
Find the 10th term from the end of 4, 9, 14, …, 254.
q.e: Counting back from 254 the AP has d = −5: 254 − 9 × 5.

q.t: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n² + 5n. Find its common difference.
Find the sum of all three-digit numbers divisible by 7.
How many terms of 15, 13, 11, … must be taken to make 60?
q.e: (n/2)(30 − 2(n − 1)) = 60 gives n² − 16n + 60 = 0, so n = 6 or 10. Both work: terms 7 to 10 (3, 1, −1, −3) add to 0.

q.t: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is 4n − n². Find its 15th term.
q.e: aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = 5 − 2n, so a₁₅ = 5 − 30.

q.t: Three numbers in AP add to 24 and multiply to 440. Find the largest.
q.e: Call them 8 − d, 8, 8 + d (they add to 24). 8(64 − d²) = 440 gives d = 3: 5, 8, 11.

q.t: In an AP, 5 times the 5th term equals 9 times the 9th term. Find the 14th term.
q.e: 5(a + 4d) = 9(a + 8d) gives a = −13d, so a₁₄ = a + 13d = 0.

q.t: An AP has 4th term 13 and 9th term 33. Find the sum of its first 15 terms.
Ravi saves ₹500 in the first month and ₹50 more each month than the month before. How much does he save in the first year (in ₹)?

q.e: These are the first 25 odd numbers, and their sum is 25².

q.t: Which term of 100, 97, 94, … is the first negative term?
An AP has 8th term 12 and 12th term 8. Find its 15th term.
q.e: Four jumps lose 4, so d = −1 and a = 19. a₁₅ = 19 − 14.

q.t: The sum of the first 6 terms of an AP is 42 and of the first 10 terms is 110. Find the sum of the first 20 terms.
The sums of n terms of two APs are in the ratio (7n + 1) : (4n + 27). Find the ratio of their 11th terms.
q.e: The 11th term ratio equals the ratio of the sums of 21 terms (n = 2 × 11 − 1): 148 : 111 = 4 : 3.

q.t: Find the sum of all two-digit odd numbers.
10 flags stand in a line 3 m apart, the first 2 m from a box. A boy runs from the box, brings back one flag at a time, and drops it in the box. How far does he run in all?
In an increasing AP, a₂ + a₆ = 10 and a₂ × a₆ = 21. Find the sum of its first 16 terms.
q.e: a₂ and a₆ are 3 and 7, so 4d = 4, d = 1, a = 2. S₁₆ = 8(4 + 15).

q.t: Find the sum of the numbers between 200 and 400 that are divisible by 7.
The sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n² + 4n. Find its 25th term.
Three numbers in AP add to 15 and their squares add to 83. Find their product.
q.e: Write them 5 − d, 5, 5 + d. Squares: 75 + 2d² = 83, so d = 2: 3, 5, 7.

q.t: The pth, qth and rth terms of an AP are a, b, c. Find a(q − r) + b(r − p) + c(p − q).
q.e: Put a = A + (p − 1)D etc. The A parts give A × 0, and the D parts cancel in pairs.

q.t: An AP has 40 terms. Its 4th term is 13 and its last term is 121. Find its 25th term.
q.e: From term 4 to term 40 is 36 jumps of 108, so d = 3 and a = 4. a₂₅ = 4 + 24 × 3.
